newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SRI LANKA SAYS NEEDS 4,000 MEGAWATT POWER BY 2015.
newsitem.headline: SRI LANKA SAYS NEEDS 4,000 MEGAWATT POWER BY 2015.

text.p: Demand for electricity in Sri Lanka is rising by 10 percent each year and the country would need to raise generation capacity to 4,000 megawatt (MW) by 2015, a senior governemnt official said on Sunday.

Jaliya Medagama, secretary of the irrigation and power ministry, made demand forecasts in special supplements carried in newspapers to mark the opening of a new 115 MW gas turbine power plant near Colombo.

"The demand for electricity is increasing by 10 percent yearly. The generation of electricity has to be doubled every seven years to fulfill this demand, said Medagama, the senior-most ministry official.
"By year 2015 we would need 4,000 MW to meet the demand."
Sri Lanka, which mostly relied on hydro-power has made a significant shift towards other forms of power generation after a drought last year crippled industry and hit the economy.
Medagama said the present hydropower generation capacity of 1,135 MW could be increased only by another 500 MW.
"During the next 10 years the thermal power stations would add 1,000 MW," he said.

Sri Lanka had until recently 250 MW of thermal capacity, mostly diesel power generation plants. It plans to build a 300 MW coal-fired plant north of the capital Colombo to meet the rising power demand.
A 115 MW Kelanitissa gas turbine power plant near Colombo was inaugurated by President Chandrika Kumaratunga on Sunday.
